items.title: The Witcher 4 Will Have a Physical Edition Even if Discs Go Away, CD Projekt Red Confirms
items.description: The Witcher 4 will still "have a box" for physical game collectors even after Sony stops supporting discs in 2028, CD Projekt Red has confirmed.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
The Witcher 4 will still "have a box" for physical game collectors even after Sony stops supporting discs in 2028, CD Projekt Red has confirmed.

Studio joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski confirmed the Cyberpunk 2077 studio still plans to release a physical edition during an interview with The Game Business. He admitted CD Projekt Red has no control when it comes to Sony's plans to halt production for physical PlayStation discs, but they do still have the power to make The Witcher 4 feel special for collectors.

"We don’t know what’s going to be the case," he said. "We know what PlayStation has announced. And we have no influence on the policies of the first parties. The discs for the first parties, including PlayStation, have to be manufactured in their own factories. So, if they stop manufacturing indeed by 2028, then yes [we won’t have a disc]."

Sony infamously announced plans to end production for physical PlayStation games in July, promising the move would take effect starting January 2028. It was a brutal blow to those who have spent decades collecting discs for their favorite games, but it will be especially painful as games previously expected to receive physical support launch without a disc.

The Witcher 4 became one of those titles when CD Projekt Red suggested it was aiming for a 2028 release date. The studio is known for packing its physical releases full of goodies for fans, too. Both standard editions for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and Cyberpunk 2077 came with the kind of bonuses you'd expect in a pricier release, including stickers, a map, a letter from the developers, postcards, and more. When Sony – and, potentially, other gaming entities – cease support for physical releases in 2028, that goes away.

Well, at least for most releases, it goes away. For CD Projekt Red, they aren't going down without a fight. While there may not be a disc for The Witcher 4, the team still wants to ensure its undated launch is just as special as the last. That's why, in some form, The Witcher 4 will "have a box."

"But we’re big fans of people having access to tangible collectible things," Nowakowski added. "We’re nerds ourselves, and we like that. We always supported that. So, whatever is the case, we’re going to be for sure having a box. We’re going to have a box that’s going to have some feelies in it. Something you’re going to be wanting to open up and enjoy. But we have no influence actually on what’s the case here."

For now, The Witcher 4 has no release date. As CD Projekt Red tinkers away at its Ciri-led Witcher 3 follow-up, you can see how the team is revitalizing its 2015 hit with an official remaster and the Songs of the Past expansion. You can also check out how both retailers and the gaming industry have lashed out at Sony over its recent decision.

items.title: Anne Hathaway Cast Opposite Tom Cruise in Days of Thunder Sequel
items.description: Anne Hathaway will star opposite Tom Cruise in the sequel to Days of Thunder. The Oscar-winning star of The Odyssey and The End of Oak Street will play a team owner and engineer in the sequel, due out summer 2028.
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
Anne Hathaway will star opposite Tom Cruise in the sequel to Days of Thunder.

Cruise announced Hathaway’s casting on social media Saturday, first by posting a teaser image of himself and Hathaway with a release date of summer 2028.

Cruise followed this with a video of himself and Hathaway wherein the Oscar-winning actress, who is pregnant, said first she’ll deliver her baby and then they’ll go make their movie.

Days of Thunder. Summer 2028. pic.twitter.com/l7tWBQVONm

— Tom Cruise (@TomCruise) August 29, 2026

Paramount Pictures followed this with an official press release, revealing that the Days of Thunder sequel will be filmed for IMAX. It will be released in theaters on premium large formats including IMAX, 4DX and Dolby Cinema on June 2, 2028:

“Tom Cruise will return as NASCAR driver Cole Trickle and will be joined by Anne Hathaway who is set to play a team owner and engineer in the upcoming follow-up to the groundbreaking 1990 film that revolutionized cinema. Cruise will star and produce alongside Jerry Bruckheimer and Tommy Harper. Jonathan Levine is set to direct from a script by Will Staples.”

Director Jonathan Levine’s past credits include 50/50, The Long Shot, Warm Bodies, The Night Before, and All the Boys Love Mandy Lane. His next film release is the fact-based sports drama Mr. Irrelevant: The John Tuggle Story, starring Superman’s David Corenswet.

Anne Hathaway can currently be seen on cinema screens in The End of Oak Street and Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey. She’ll next be seen in the thriller Verity. Hathaway’s other releases this year include The Devil Wears Prada 2 and Mother Mary.

Days of Thunder. Summer 2028. pic.twitter.com/rD3QLXfUyi

— Tom Cruise (@TomCruise) August 29, 2026

Tom Cruise will next be seen in director Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s apocalyptic comedy Digger, which Cruise has called “totally original” and unlike any other film he’s ever made.

IGN named the original Days of Thunder among the 15 best racing movies of all time.

items.title: Ridley Scott Says Alien: Romulus 'Was OK,' So He's Returning to the Franchise Because It 'Needs Some Help'
items.description: Director Ridley Scott said Alien: Romulus "was OK," so he's returning to the Alien franchise because it "needs some help."
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Director Ridley Scott said Alien: Romulus "was OK," so he's returning to the Alien franchise because it "needs some help."

The director behind classic movies like Blade Runner and the original Alien, as well as the newly released The Dog Stars, made his feelings about the direction the sci-fi series is heading in during an interview with French outlet AlloCiné (via Deadline). During the conversation, Scott again confirmed that he's "gone back in" to the property that helped put him on the map.

The reason? He thinks Alien: Romulus could have been better.

"I'm rewriting the next Alien film," Scott explained. "Actually, I suddenly went back and got involved. The one that just came out [2024's Alien: Romulus], it was OK. I think it needs some help. So, I've gone back in."

Alien: Romulus served as a soft reboot for the Alien universe by plopping new characters like Rain (Cailee Spaeny), Andy the android (David Jonsson), and Kay (Isabela Merced) into a story polluted by Xenomorphs, Facehuggers, and if you made it to the end of the film, something…else. It was generally favorably reviewed, with aggregator Rotten Tomatoes reporting an 80% critic score and an 85% audience score.

IGN gave it an 8/10 review. We said its "back-to-basics approach to blockbuster horror boils everything fans love about the tonally-fluid franchise into one brutal, nerve-wracking experience."

For Scott's tastes, however, it seems it simply wasn't enough. It's strange, considering that film's director, Fede Álvarez, said Scott told him it was "f**king great" after watching an early cut.

It's worth noting that Scott does refer to the project in question as "the one that just came out." It's possible he could be referring to 2025's TV show, Alien: Earth, but he does make his comment after referring to the films, suggesting it's Alien: Romulus that's got him wanting to be involved again. For reference, Alien: Earth also landed with a positive reception, earning a 94% from critics and a 65% from audiences.

Either way, Scott wants to be more hands-on. He recently confirmed he was working to continue the trilogy he started with 2012's Prometheus and 2017's Alien: Covenant with a new film starring Michael Fassbender's David. The plan is to see the character "create a brave new world for himself" while tackling the topic of AI. He teased more of his ideas during the new interview.

"I've already got a footprint for the next Alien," he continued. "We did Prometheus and Covenant, so I'm picking up where we left in Covenant. [David], who now thinks he's Ozymandias, is going [circles finger by head].

"I like the fact that AI is going off the rails. If we go AI, the moment we discover it's off the rails, it's too late. It could switch every digital thing off in the world like that. You'd have f**king chaos. It's that kind of stuff that's scary."

Scott is currently encouraging audiences to check out The Dog Stars, which came to theaters yesterday, August 28, 2026. It's a film adaptation of the post-apocalyptic book of the same name and stars Jacob Elordi, Margaret Qualley, and Josh Brolin. When his proposed Alien trilogy cap will premiere, however, remains a mystery.

David is coming back, but Rain and Andy's future remains uncertain. A proper Alien: Romulus sequel was announced to be in the works in November 2024. Although Álvarez was said to be in talks to return to direct, with Scott also confirming he would be in the mix at the time, it was reported in September of last year that Álvarez would only be involved as a producer.

Photo by Kristy Sparow/Getty Images for Disney.

items.title: Join Us: Watch 11 Minutes of Exclusive Gameplay from the Upcoming Cult Simulator | gamescom 2026
items.description: Wolf Haus Games revealed 11 minutes of gameplay for Join Us at gamescom 2026, alongside a PS5 announcement and a trailer featuring real-life former cult members.
items.author: Adam Bankhurst
items.content:
Join Us, the upcoming open-world co-op game where you can start your very own doomsday cult, just dropped a ton of new gameplay as part of IGN's gamescom programming. You can see more than 11 minutes of exclusive footage in the player below, and get a deeper look into just how the game will work.

Earlier this week, developer Wolf Haus games announced that the darkly satirical survival/action cult simulator will be available on PS5 at launch alongside the PC and Xbox Series X/S versions in March 2027. The news of Join Us' PS5 version also featured information on how 4-player co-op will work in both the campaign and free roam.

In addition to the extended gameplay, IGN can exclusively reveal a special video from Wolf Haus showing four real-life former cult members coming together to play Join Us in co-op and reflicting on their past histories while enjoying this new adventure and reacting to the game

The live-action trailer featuring former cult members, which you can watch below, introduces us to Jaga, Javier, Ariel, and Elena - who have a "collective experience of over 50 years in their unique societies." This experience involves a cult that is preparing for aliens to arrive on Earth and take us back to the planet we came from, a peaceful cult that focuses on martial arts and self-defense training, and a holistic rejuvenation cult.

In Join Us, players will need to stay vigilant though, as they'll need to keep their recruits happy or they will leave the cult. As the devs put it, "a cult leader without any followers is just a lonely weirdo."

For more from gamescom, be sure to check out everything that was revealed during Opening Night Live.

items.title: The Pokémon Company Looks to Smart Device Integrations as Future Targets
items.description: President and CEO of The Pokémon Company, Tsunekazu Ishihara, shared a small bit of insight about the company’s possible future plans with wearable technology during a panel discussion at the inaugural PokémonXP.
items.author: Casey DeFreitas
items.content:
President and CEO of The Pokémon Company, Tsunekazu Ishihara, shared a small bit of insight about the company’s possible future plans with wearable technology during a panel discussion at the inaugural PokémonXP in San Francisco, CA.

During the Producing Pokémon: A Conversation with Mr. Ishihara panel at the main PokémonXP stage, Ishihara spoke about how Pokémon has evolved alongside major technological shifts in handheld gaming and wireless connectivity over the years. He said after smartphones arrived, they had to change their approach a little to accessories.

“In the past, these gadgets or companion accessories [like the Pokéwalker and PokémonGO Plus] were kind of like these cool secret weapons you could pull out of your pocket and do something really cool with,” Ishihara said, “but today I was thinking, going forward, maybe a challenge for us is going to be figuring out how we can integrate Pokémon more with some of the wearable technology, like smart watches, smart glasses, or even smart rings, for example.”
The comment comes on the tail of the reveal of the Fitbit Air Special Edition Pokémon Sleep, a wearable health tracker with full connectivity to Pokémon Sleep, a Pokémon app that essentially gamifies sleep into collecting Pokémon.

Ishihara is also the founder and previous CEO of Creatures Inc., a co-owner of the Pokémon franchise alongside Nintendo and Game Freak, who together make The Pokémon Company International. Ishihara has experienced the complete history of the franchise, from Pokémon Red and Pokémon Green to the conception of the anime and trading card game. During the panel, Ishihara said he’s always loved handheld gadgets and toys and is particularly passionate about them.

“I really hope Pokémon and the people who are stewarding it will continue to be creating entirely new forms of play that really excite people. And also that humanity, in general, will continue to really enjoy those experiences. And maybe even across three or four generations in the future,” Ishihara said.

Casey DeFreitas is the deputy editor of guides at IGN, and has attended the Pokémon World Championships since 2017. She's here at PokémonXP! Catch her on socials @ShinyCaseyD, and at Worlds!

items.title: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil on Track to Have Biggest Opening Weekend of Any RE Movie in History
items.description: Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie is on track to have the most profitable opening weekend out of any film adaptation of Capcom’s flagship horror franchise.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie is on track to have the most profitable opening weekend out of any film adaptation of Capcom’s flagship horror franchise.

Stats aggregated by Box Office Pro, a business-to-business trade magazine and the official publication of the National Association of Theater Owners, are giving optimistic predictions for Cregger’s Resident Evil.

The zombie flick is projected to earn $40M – $50M during its opening weekend this September — an amount that would make it the most financially successful opening weekend for any Resident Evil movie ever released in theaters.

For comparison, the highest amount earned during an opening weekend for a Resident Evil movie was for Resident Evil: Afterlife, which netted $26,650,26 when it opened in 2010.

Resident Evil: Apocalypse and Resident Evil: Extinction both earned around $23 million during their opening weekends. The original RE movie, released in 2002, scored $17.7 million for its opening weekend, with the lowest amount going to 2021’s Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City. (That’s not too surprising; the film was widely panned by fans and critics alike, with IGN giving it a 6 out of 10 at the time.)

Enthusiasm for Cregger’s take on the series is at an all-time high, even though the famous filmmaker has publicly eschewed the idea of creating a 1:1 adaptation of the games. Rather than trying to live up to what fans have already played, Cregger follows an average Joe who gets caught up in the Racoon City Incident — and so far, it’s looking pretty solid.

Cregger has included more than a few cheeky references to the games (the main character scrambling for ammo, Heavy Field shotgun shells from Resident Evil 4, first-person action sequences, a typewriter and the mention of Umbrella), and considering his impressive resume of highly-lauded horror films (Barbarian, Weapons), this fresh take on the beloved video game franchise experiencing a good about of hype.

Speaking with IGN at San Diego Comic Con, Cregger explained why he chose to pursue a different approach than most fans likely expected, admitting that he “took liberties” with the source material.

“I am not trying to adapt a video game,” he told us. I'm not using the characters from the games. I'm not telling a story that the games tell because I'm not going to be able to do it better than the games. The games are so well executed, and to me, Leon and Claire and these characters, they exist so perfectly in the games that anyone I cast and any difference that I do with them would be, probably, to the detriment of what I was trying to do."

Cregger’s Resident Evil has been described as an "all gas, no brakes" thrill ride and the "Fury Road of horror." At one hour and 35 minutes long, we’d expect nothing less, and we’re keen to see if box office predictions line up when September 18 finally rolls around.

Image credit: CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze.

items.title: Xbox CEO Says Project Helix Includes a 'Family of Devices'
items.description: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has suggested Project Helix will encompass more than one device, saying that Microsoft has been working on "a great family of devices."
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has suggested Project Helix will encompass more than one device, saying that Microsoft has been working on "a great family of devices."

As Microsoft attempts to navigate mass layoffs across its gaming branch, the company has mostly played its cards close to the chest when it comes to its mysterious next-gen Xbox console. Project Helix was formally announced with the promise of PC game-playing capabilities back in March of this year, and now Sharma may be teasing something more.

The Xbox CEO teased some of what's to come for Project Helix during an interview with the BBC at gamescom 2026. While Microsoft wants to stay tight-lipped, some of what she had to say suggested the gaming hardware might be more than a simple box release.

"We're not sharing more on Helix, I know you had to ask it," Sharma said when asked if Project Helix will be a "discless" console. "But look, we've been hard at work on a great next generation and a great family of devices for Helix, and we'll share more soon."

With so little to go on, Sharma's comment could mean a lot of things. This past generation, for example, saw the release of not one but two Xbox consoles with its Series X/S releases. The X, considered a more powerful device, features a disc drive, while the S is an all-digital device.

The mention of a "family of devices" for Project Helix doesn't exactly mean that there will be something like a Project Helix Series X/S, but it does suggest Microsoft may be preparing for a next-gen console that could be just as untraditional as the one it follows.

Despite Sharma suggesting in the past that Project Helix may be targeting a holiday 2027 release, we don't know exactly when the new gaming hardware will launch. In June, she acknowledged that a mass audience won't be willing to spend "thousands of dollars" on a "console generation," teasing that Microsoft will explore "new business models" as it looks to the future.

While we wait to see what exactly Project Helix and its family of devices are, you can see why we think the next-gen Xbox console needs to clearly communicate its strengths and be more than a simple Series sequel. While it's unclear if it will allow fans to use physical game discs in a traditional sense, what is clear is that Microsoft will soon allow Xbox fans to digitize their video games.

items.title: The Founders of Hooters Are Making a Buddy-Comedy Movie About the Restaurant Chain's Origin Story
items.description: Yep, you read that right. Hooters: The Movie is in the early stages of pre-production, and some of the chain’s original founders are directly involved.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Yep, you read that right. Hooters: The Movie is in the early stages of pre-production, and some of the chain’s original founders are directly involved.

As reported by Deadline, the film is inspired by the “real events” behind Hooters’ creation, following best buds Ted and Lenny as they create a sprawling legacy for themselves with their famous ‘breastaurant’ chain — only to have their life’s work jeopardized by the US government.

Ted falls head over heels for a gal named Diane after seeing her on a TV commercial. Ted convinces Lenny to drive down with him to Clearwater Beach, Florida, where they recruit Diane to become the original Hooters Girl. The flick is described as part buddy comedy, part biopic that tells the “wild journey” of how the iconic American eatery got its start.

One of Hooters’ co-founders, Edward Droste, is both producing the film and co-authoring its screenplay. Jon Rosenbaum (Benchwarmers 2: Breaking Balls) is set to direct, and casting is already underway. Filming is scheduled to begin in November in Florida's Tampa and Clearwater areas, which is where the very first Hooters restaurant opened its doors all the way back in 1983.

“I think people are going to enjoy watching how we were really just some guys who didn’t know what we were doing, but had a great time doing it,” Droste said in a press release. “And of course, our world-famous Hooters Girls are the real stars. It’s time to deliver a taste of our big-hearted culture and famous humor to the world.”

“From the moment I first learned the Hooters origin story, I knew it would make an incredible movie,” Rosenbaum remarked. “It’s the perfect combination of a hilarious buddy comedy and an inspiring biopic for a beloved American brand: Two lifelong friends with no idea what they’re getting themselves into, a crazy idea they’re willing to bet everything on, and a wild journey that culminates in the creation of something bigger than they could ever have imagined. It’s not at all what people will be expecting – and it’s mostly true! I can’t wait to bring this story to life.”

If you’re unfamiliar, Hooters is a casual dining / sports bar chain known for its wings and its waitresses, young ladies who are often clad in white t-shirts and orange shorts. The chain was actually founded by six people: Lynn D. Stewart, Gil DiGiannantonio, Ed Droste. Billy Ranieri, Ken Wimmer, and Dennis Johnson.

At the time of writing, there are around 200 locations within the US, and 60 internationally in areas including the Bahamas, the Czech Republic, Japan, Switzerland, and more.

Image credits: David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images

items.title: [UPDATE] Indie Dev Posts Video Reporting Stolen Laptops at gamescom as CD Projekt Red and More Step in to Help
items.description: Ryan Laley, the solo indie developer behind upcoming asymmetrical horror game Mimic, has shared a video confirming his gamescom was "cut short" after he and other developers had their laptops stolen.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
UPDATE AUGUST 29, 2026: Both gamescom and Mimic developer Ryan Laley have responded to IGN's request for comment.

gamescom organizers replied to IGN's email request, pointing to a general statement regarding incidents of theft at this year's show. The same message was also posted to social media. You can read it in its entirety below.

"We are aware of stolen hardware and take these reports very seriously and understand the frustration of affected exhibitors," the message said. "Since many requests reached us, we would like to inform about general security regulations at the event: Uniformed guards provide general security across the venue. Individual stand security can be booked separately, and exhibitors are advised to insure equipment against theft.

"This is noted in the terms and conditions of participation and the technical guidelines. All cases have been reported to us and to the police, and investigations are already underway. We also want to ensure that the reported cases are individual cases, which we are very sorry to read. Because security has one of the highest priorities to us as an event and to see that indie developers are affected makes us very sad.

"At an event of this size, however, there will always be individuals attempting to take advantage of the situation. Our security measures are designed to minimize such risks as effectively as possible."

We are aware of stolen hardware and take these reports very seriously and understand the frustration of affected exhibitors.

Since many requests reached us, we would like to inform about general security regulations at the event:
Uniformed guards provide general security across…

— gamescom (@gamescom) August 29, 2026

Laley also replied to IGN's request to learn more about both his stolen equipment and the events that followed. He clarified that it was his Alienware 16X Aurora gaming laptop that was taken, resulting in at least one full day of canceled appointments and missed opportunities. In his own words, it's the kind of thing that can leave a solo deveveloper feeling "isolated and vulnerable."

Thankfully, Laley wasn't alone for too long. After posting his first video following the incident, he was met with a wave of support from the gaming industry. He said he started the day "feeling sick" and "defeated," saying he wanted to "just go home and throw in the towel." He added that seeing everyone lend a hand "warmed my heart greatly."

"Words can't describe it," Laley told us. "I was simply sharing what happened to my existing community as I teach game Dev on YouTube and mentor studios and individuals as my main job. To see the explosion of love and support has been unreal and unbelievable. I'm glad to raise a spotlight to security concerns that other have had too and encourage everyone to look out for each other."

The indie dev has yet to receive any specific updates regarding his stolen gear. He was told he likely won't hear from police for another six weeks.

Laley has received significant support from his peers and fans alike. He asks any others hoping to help him make up lost ground check out Mimic on Steam, while encouraging those interested in development with Unreal technology to head over to his YouTube channel.

"Support the indie Devs," he added. "Making games is hard work, they/we are trying to share our love of this craft. We don't have a budget of some studios and are often paying out of pocket for a lot of this. So please go support the other developers out there too. They deserve it."

ORIGINAL STORY AUGUST 28, 2026: Ryan Laley, the solo indie developer behind upcoming asymmetrical horror game Mimic, has shared a video confirming his gamescom was "cut short" after he and other developers had their laptops stolen.

A teary Laley took to X/Twitter to share a video explaining why his "gamescom is over early," saying that "all our laptops have been stolen" after he and others had their booths "raided" overnight. Bringing Mimic to the Cologne, Germany gaming event meant getting the opportunity to show it off to a new audience of potential partners and eager gamers alike, but stolen gear would bring that dream to an end.

"As an indie, solo dev, this s**t's expensive and hard to do all by yourself," he said. "And to have this happen is beyond frustrating – it's heartbreaking."

My #gamescom cut short. Our equipment was stolen last night from the booth.

Police reports have been filed.

At a loss for words to describe the feeling. Just defeated. Gonna do my best with what's left of the week.

But a huge blow financially and mentally pic.twitter.com/dKpp3Of6df

— Mimic | Ryan Laley (@RyanLaley) August 28, 2026

Laley went on, saying the gamescom theft was reported to the proper security teams and authorities. Despite the effort he and others were putting in, he noted, "I don't expect it, obviously, to be found or returned."

"I don't know what I'm going to do now," he added. "I can't do my job. We'll post updates if I get any updates, but effectively, gamescom is over for me."

gamescom kicked off when Opening Night Live (ONL) aired Tuesday, August 25, letting developers loose for the rest of the week to show what they bring to the table. At the time of this story's publication, there are still more than two days left in the show, making Laley's loss an especially painful one. Thankfully, his story and video gained enough traction to reach the eyes of developers looking to help.

The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 team at CD Projekt Red quickly chimed in, apologizing to Laley for the circumstances he'd been thrust into. They admitted they wouldn't be able to "help right this second," but they did promise to "send a few things" his way.

"No choom should have to start from zero," its post said.

Gaming industry expert and Don't Scream developer Joe Henson (a.k.a. Indie Game Joe) went as far as to post a video message reply offering his support. It's an offer that Laley seems to have accepted.

Thank you for the support everyone. Long crazy day.

I'm still around this weekend if you want to catch up at Gamescom. I'll be boothless but still in my Mimic shirt (a fresh one DW) so come say hi if you see me :)

Looking forward to meeting other Devs and trying out their… pic.twitter.com/b0gro1BL0Y

— Mimic | Ryan Laley (@RyanLaley) August 28, 2026

Thank you everyone for outpouring of love and support today! You are the reason why I love this industry

❤️

— Mimic | Ryan Laley (@RyanLaley) August 28, 2026

"Thank you everyone so much for your support and love," he said in a follow-up post. "I'm trying to say thanks to everyone, but honestly, my fingers aren't fast enough. Huge shout-out and thanks to @IndieGameJoe, who kindly donated the money to replace my stolen hardware. He truly is a champion for the little guys, and [I'm] so thankful for his support towards all of us indies!"

Laley returned with an additional post later, thanking everyone again for their support. Although he will no longer have his booth, he still encouraged anyone interested in Mimic to find him at gamescom.

"Words can't describe how much I'm grateful for everyone's support," he said. "I'm a mentor and trainer in Unreal Engine, I train a lot of people up and go to a lot of universities, talk to a lot of students who want to get into games, and one of the things I always say to them is how friendly and warm and supportive of each other it is. Today is just evident of that. Proof that you guys are amazing."

Today at gamescom we arrived to our station in the business area hall to discover that our two laptops had been stolen over night, despite the presence of Koelnmesse security.

These were machines we were using to demo iam8bit Presents titles Petal Runner and Escape Academy 2 to…

— iam8bit @ gamescom hall 5.2 stand C051 (@iam8bit) August 28, 2026

We were robbed at Gamescom.

On Wednesday, we arrived at our booth in the Indie Area to find our cabinet forced open. Two laptops and a Steam Deck were gone.

The devices contained not only our Gamescom demo, but also personal, company, and critical information.

Here’s our story pic.twitter.com/ZghaSx9RJB

— The Zibbo Show ➡️ Wishlist on Steam 💥 (@tesserastudios) August 28, 2026

Unfortunately, Laley was far from the only person affected by thieves at gamescom. Publisher and pop-culture collectible company iam8bit shared its own message reporting stolen goods at gamescom, saying that it had two laptops taken overnight. It added that, "on top of disrupting our very busy appointment schedule, this theft has potentially put unfinished builds of these games at risk of being leaked."

Tessera Studios, which is working on the game show-inspired The Zibbo Show, also published a video announcing it had been "robbed at gamescom." They called the damage it's caused the team "pretty huge."

For now, gamescom organizers have yet to publicly comment on the reports of theft at the event. IGN has reached out for comment.

items.title: Kick Streamer Neon Responds After Rockstar Seemingly Includes a Reference to Him in GTA 6 Netflix Showcase
items.description: Prominent Kick streamer Neon has responded after Rockstar appeared to reference him in a side mission shown during their special GTA 6 first-look trailer on Netflix.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Prominent Kick streamer Neon has responded after Rockstar appeared to reference him in a side mission shown during their special GTA 6 first-look trailer on Netflix.

Rockstar broke the internet yesterday when it premiered 26 minutes of gameplay footage from Grand Theft Auto 6 on Netflix, causing brief issues on the platform and even on Twitch, where a number of streamers were reacting to the showcase in real time.

Speaking of streamers, the highly-anticipated showcase featured a side mission where Lucia steals a car — only for a content creator to hop out of the trunk after the heist is finished, asking his viewers, “Holy sh*t chat, what do I do?”

Fans couldn’t help but notice a striking resemblance between the fictional influencer and a real-life streamer named Neon. The two boast similar features and even have the same style of haircut, prompting netizens to recreate that Leonardo DiCaprio meme as they watched the preview from home.

Neon went live on Kick the next day, where he officially addressed the topic — and while he didn’t provide any solid confirmation that he truly was the inspiration for GTA 6’s streamer character, he did thank his audience for getting him popular enough to make it a legitimate theory.

"We made it! We f**kin’ did it!” an excited Neon said as he sat in the back of a car. “Shout out to everyone in the chat. I've seen some reactions: A lot of people weren't the happiest, a lot of people were showing support.

“Two streamers did text me. You know who you are, and I appreciate you. Thank you guys. …Would a B-Tier streamer really be in [this game]? Nah, I’m just kidding. That is f**kin’ sick, bro! Streaming is really taking over the game. I'm just so happy and blessed and grateful to even be seen like that, in that way.”

items.title: Rockstar Approached Netflix for Exclusive GTA 6 Extended Look, Not the Other Way Around
items.description: The big Grand Theft Auto 6 extended look (mostly) went off without a hitch, and apparently, it was Rockstar Games' idea to bring it to Netflix in the first place, not the other way around.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
The big Grand Theft Auto 6 extended look (mostly) went off without a hitch, and apparently, it was Rockstar Games' idea to bring it to Netflix in the first place, not the other way around.

Amidst the unprecedented amount of hype for GTA 6, there was a fair amount of confusion from fans, who questioned Rockstar's decision to make its gameplay debut a Netflix exclusive for six hours after its premiere yesterday. This first real look at Jason and Lucia's story definitely managed to wow viewers, but even after 27 minutes of Vice City, the question remained: Why Netflix?

Many assumed it to be a high-value deal cooked up by the streaming giant to pull eyes its way, but apparently, that's not the case. A Rockstar PR representative told Kinda Funny Games ahead of the big reveal that it was actually the GTA 6 developer's idea to stream the extended look on Netflix. The quote is: "We wanted to go to Netflix."

It's a response that may generate more questions than answers. Rockstar first raised eyebrows when it confirmed plans to bring GTA 6: Extended Look exclusively to Netflix earlier this month, promising what eventually turned out to be a lengthy version of a long-awaited third trailer – but only for subscribers. Even with the knowledge that the full presentation would eventually drop on YouTube just a few hours later, fans who have been waiting 13 years for the next Grand Theft Auto were annoyed to hear they'd have to wait even longer if they didn't want to fork over the cash.

"This is unbelievably scummy," said one fan on X at the time. "Everyone is excited for the extended look of GTA 6, but it's premiering on Netflix first, which will influence people to get a subscription. This needs to be called out, because if any other studio, such as Bethesda, did this, they would be crucified."

Still, some were willing to be patient and see if there might be something more to Rockstar's grand plan. At least some of the hesitation then turned to excitement after Strauss Zelnick, CEO of parent company Take-Two Interactive, promised that the extended look would be worth the price for early admission.

He went as far as to say that the plan was "an example of Rockstar trying new things" as marketing for GTA 6 truly kicked off. He also told Bloomberg, "I think when the title is launched on Netflix, if you watch it, you'll understand more."

"If you're not a Netflix subscriber, you definitely should be one," he told IGN at the time. "And as for the trailer itself, it's coming soon enough that I'll let you arrive at your own conclusion."

Well, the trailer is here, and while it certainly managed to impress, it's still not clear why Rockstar felt the need to bring GTA 6: Extended Look to Netflix, specifically. That said, there are still months to go before launch arrives. Nothing about the developer's future marketing plans has been revealed yet, so it's possible we could see other entries or even episodes added to Extended Look in the future.

For now, though, all we know is that Rockstar has its reasons. IGN got an early peak at all things GTA 6 ahead of yesterday's gameplay reveal and walked away just about as impressed as everyone else. You can check out our thoughts in our preview, and then be sure to see what we had to ask the developer in our interview. You can also check out 69 details we learned while visiting Rockstar HQ, the GTA Online character who's making a comeback, and the Red Dead Redemption 2 Easter Egg hidden in the extended look.

items.title: Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d and Pichu Will Be Exclusive to Disney+
items.description: The upcoming stop-motion series will stream exclusively on Disney+ and DisneyXD, as revealed in a special showcase during PokémonXP.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The upcoming stop-motion series will stream exclusively on Disney+ and DisneyXD, as revealed in a special showcase during PokémonXP.

PokémonXP is underway, marking the debut of the very first fan convention completely dedicated to all-things Pokémon. Of course, some exclusive reveals and big announcements are expected, and one of those involves the brand’s next big animated series.

First announced in July 2025, The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d and Pichu is exactly what it sounds like — a charming, humorous romp that follows the two Pokémon as they get into all sorts of hijinks in Galar.

As revealed at PokémonXP, the series will be streamed exclusively on Disney+ and the DisneyXD channel. This was an unexpected turn of events, as the brand’s first stop motion series, Pokémon Concierge, streams solely on Netflix.

This new show is being made in collaboration between The Pokémon Company International and Aardman Animations, the British stop-motion animation studio best known for beloved properties like Wallace and Gromit and Shaun the Sheep.

As told during the show’s behind-the-scenes panel at PokémonXD, there are 262 people working on the project at any given time. Each animator achieves roughly 13.5 seconds of animation per week, with each episode taking 110 weeks to complete. Three episodes are usually in production simultaneously, allowing the crew to get as much work done as possible.

Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d & Pichu, our new stop-motion animated series with @aardman, is coming to @DisneyPlusUK in 2027! 🛡️⚡

Join our unlikely heroes, Sirfetch’d and Pichu, in their gallant quest to protect Pokémon across Galar. pic.twitter.com/D3UBkZ3pBE

— Pokémon UK (@PokemonNewsUK) August 28, 2026

The panel also showed off the very first animation tests for both Pichu and SirFetch’d, as well as an official trailer for the show, which will release sometime in 2027.

The series' official logline reads: "Our heroes embark on a gallant quest to help and protect Pokémon across the region. Their missions rarely go as planned, but their noble deeds forge their friendship as they step bravely into the unknown. Peril, alliances, rivalries, extraordinary Pokémon, and endless laughs await them."

As told by the folks at Aardman, Escavalier will serve as the main antagonist of the series, which they described as a “knight that could challenge and compete against” Sirfetch’d.

“What I love is the personalities we’re giving to all these characters," James Young of Aardman Animations said. "I'm really excited for the Pokémon family, and for all of you and to see how you like them, to see the personalities we’ve given to these Pokémon characters in our world."

Pokémon Concierge was also confirmed for a second season back in 2025, set to air on Netflix this September.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Is Already Bringing Back Characters from GTA 5
items.description: Grand Theft Auto 6 will feature at least one character from GTA Online.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto 6 will feature at least one character from GTA Online.

In Rockstar's extended look at GTA 6, fans were introduced to a bunch of characters with a wide range of morals. One character that fans probably overlooked is Valentina, a woman who was introduced last year in GTA Online. She makes her debut in a cutscene for the Money Fronts update, where she can be seen hopping off a private jet and interacting with Mr. Faber. While her role didn't seem especially significant at the time, it looks like she'll have a larger part to play in GTA 6.

The character hires Jason and Lucia to be security for a VIP who is attending a party that is inevitably disrupted by gun-wielding goons. It's unclear if Valentina will have a larger role in GTA 6 outside of this mission, but it wouldn't be surprising if she did. It also raises the question of what else, or who else, Rockstar has been planting in GTA Online all these years. Of course, fans are hopeful to see Michael, Franklin, and Trevor return in GTA 6, but it remains to be seen if that will actually happen.

Valentina is the first GTA Online character confirmed to return in GTA 6.#GTAVI pic.twitter.com/CbzzQAudDF

— GTA Wiki (@GTAWikiOfficial) August 27, 2026

GTA 5 and GTA Online featured a handful of characters from GTA 4, including Brucie, Karen, Packie, and more. It wouldn't be surprising if Rockstar continues this same strategy and we see small side characters from the previous games in GTA 6. We likely won't get definitive answers on this until release, but this small reveal will certainly lead to rampant speculation.

In related news, IGN has heaps of other GTA 6-related news following the extended look. We got an exclusive preview of the game, an interview with Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson, and a variety of breakdowns on the game's various systems and details. Rockstar also confirmed that GTA 6 playthroughs can last as long as 80 hours, if not even longer, so you can expect to spend an outrageous amount of time in Leonida when the game releases in November.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

items.title: Chun-Li Actress Grew Her Thighs 6.5cm to Match the First Lady of Fighting Games for the Street Fighter Movie
items.description: Callina Liang, who plays Chun-Li in Legendary’s upcoming Street Fighter movie, revealed the protein-heavy diet and intense workout routine she followed to bring the First Lady of Fighting Games to life.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Callina Liang, who plays Chun-Li in Legendary’s upcoming Street Fighter movie, revealed the protein-heavy diet and intense workout routine she followed to bring the First Lady of Fighting Games to life.

If there’s one thing Chun-Li is known for — besides being the Strongest Woman in the World, of course — it’s her thick, muscular thunder thighs, which have only gotten more impressive with each new Street Fighter game. From Third Strike to Street Fighter V and now Street Fighter 6, it’s clear the devs at Capcom have a clear vision in mind for the character’s physical appearance. (And we thank them for it.)

Callina Liang knew this was an important thing to get right, so she buckled down and began following a strict martial arts workout routine and eating a high-protein diet to help grow her muscles — to the point where she almost got sick.

"Chun-Li is all kicks. So we did a bunch of Taekwondo training, Muay Thai, and Wushu (Kung Fu). I did two hours of that a day and strengthened my legs a lot and changed my diet drastically. When I was bulking, I ate 12 eggs a day. Every two hours I had to have a meal, and I was on the verge of throwing up. But it worked. By the end of the shoot, my thighs had grown six-and-a-half centimeters each,” she said in an August interview with Empire Magazine.

That’s not all; Liang did her homework and downloaded every single Street Fighter game onto her PlayStation 5, where she recorded all of the character’s moves to make her fight scenes as accurate as possible.

"I downloaded every single version of Street Fighter onto a PS5 and I recorded all of Chun-Li's moves during fights on my phone in slow-mo, so I could play them back and study them," she added.

Liang isn’t the only actor who put in major time to make their Street Fighter performance perfect; David Dastmalchian, who plays the series’ recurring villain, M. Bison, told us that he did deep research to deliver a version of the psycho-powered dictator that leans heavily into a cult-leader archetype.

“I don’t want to be just another one of these bad guys, cut from the typical cloth,” he said. “How do you have all of these people willing to go into battle for you, die for you? …we dug in and studied really insane dictators over time, thinking about everyone from idamine all the way back to fascist Italy in World War II, and looking at not just movie characters but real, historical characters,” he said during a chat with IGN’s Tom Jorgensen at San Diego Comic-Con.

Legendary’s Street Fighter flick releases in theaters on October 16, 2026. It’ll be the second Capcom property getting a theatrical release this year, with Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil beginning screenings on September 18.

items.title: Capcom Is Making Life-Sized Statues of Lady Dimitrescu and Albert Wesker, and the Internet Is Being Totally Normal About It
items.description: Capcom is making thirsty fans’ dreams come true for Resident Evil’s 30th anniversary exhibition, revealing that it will display life-sized statues of Lady Dimitrescu and Albert Wesker.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Capcom is making thirsty fans’ dreams come true for Resident Evil’s 30th anniversary exhibition, revealing that it will display life-sized statues of Lady Dimitrescu and Albert Wesker.

There’s something for everyone at Capcom’s RE anniversary extravaganza. Coming to the Shibuya BEAM Gallery from October 30 to December 24, the exhibition will feature real-life recreations of iconic items and creatures from the famous horror game franchise, including “life-sized models of villains crafted with meticulous detail,” as told by SaigaNAK.

Two of these villains have been revealed, and the reactions from the internet have not disappointed.

items.title: [UPDATE] EA Motive Confirms Iron Man Game Leak After Gameplay Trailer Spreads on Social Media
items.description: Gameplay footage from what appears to be EA Motive Studio's Iron Man game has leaked online.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
UPDATE AUGUST 28, 2026: EA has confirmed the Iron Man game leak is real, teasing that it has "a lot more to show" in the future.

The publisher confirmed Motive Studio's Iron Man game leaked online today in a statement sent to Kotaku. It also directed viewers to a new X/Twitter account created in the aftermath of the leak. You can see its first post below.

"Well, that didn't go as planned," EA's post said. "But now you know, and we've got a lot more to show you. See you when we're ready."

Well, that didn't go as planned. But now you know, and we've got a lot more to show you. See you when we’re ready. pic.twitter.com/tU4TtUoZYZ

— Iron Man (@PlayIronManGame) August 28, 2026

ORIGINAL STORY: Gameplay footage from what appears to be EA Motive Studio's Iron Man game has leaked online.

Video for what seems to be EA's long-in-development Iron Man game started circulating on social media today. It's a bit more than a few cobbled-together clips, too, showing a (very unfinished) project that features not only Tony Stark's Iron Man, but what seem to be a S.H.I.E.L.D. helicarrier and potentially other characters that Marvel fans may recognize.

The footage, which appeaers to be part of a trailer from an early-in-development build, looks like the kind of thing you'd expect from an Iron Man game. Tony can be seen flying under bridges and through city streets, beating up armored bad guys in between shots of him tinkering on new suit technology, giving the impression that EA Motive is crafting something that will have players traveling around the world.

The allegedly leaked footage for the Iron Man game promises that players will be shooting missiles, using arm-mounted lasers, and throwing missiles at tanks. We won't share any of that here, but if the footage does turn out to be real, it would seem rumors that Motive's Iron Man game was canceled have been greatly exaggerated.

Interestingly, this isn't even the first time this week footage for an unfinished Iron Man game found its way on the net. Monday, video for what seemed to be Avalanche Studios' Iron Man game also surfaced online. It's a different project that was rumored to be in development in the early 2010s before its eventual cancellation. While that team's vision will never see the light of day, nothing is suggesting EA's Iron Man will meet the same fate.

Motive officially revealed its take on the character almost exactly four years ago in 2022. Despite the immense amount of hype the Dead Space remake and Star Wars: Squadrons developer managed to generate at the time, things have been distressingly quiet since.

Our last real update arrived in April 2024, when the team reassured fans that its Iron Man game remained an "important priority" as EA brought it in to work on Battlefield 6. With little else besides a teaser image to keep fans occupied, some had started to worry the team's Marvel project may have kicked the can. However, for now, the game is still officially considered to very much be in development.

"In parallel, development continues to move forward on our Iron Man project, led by Olivier Proulx (Executive Producer) and Ian Frazier (Creative Director)," Motive general manager Patrick Klaus said in 2024. "The team made excellent progress this year, hitting a major internal milestone and laying a robust foundation for the journey ahead. Iron Man is an important priority for Motive, and I’m very proud of the work we’ve accomplished so far."

While it's unclear when footage from today's supposed leak would have been captured, it suggests Motive has been steadily moving along behind the scenes. In an environment where fans clamor for Spider-Man and Wolverine video games, an Iron Man game could (hopefully) have a lot of potential. EA had no comment to share when contacted by IGN.

While we wait for updates as Motive hammers away at its Iron Man game, you can check out the Tony Stark-themed popcorn buckets revealed for the upcoming Avengers: Endgame re-release. You can also check out our review of the VR game that released in 2020.

items.title: Xbox Anniversary Consoles Sell for Thousands on eBay as Scalpers Cash In on X25
items.description: The Xbox Series X25 anniversary console is officially up for pre-order, so you know what that means: scalpers are cashing in.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
The Xbox Series X25 anniversary console is officially up for pre-order, so you know what that means: scalpers are cashing in.

Like clockwork, pre-order pages for Microsoft's 25th anniversary console were bombarded by buyers when they went live yesterday, August 27, 2026. At $899.99 for that translucent green box and $79.99 for its themed controller, the price to celebrate Xbox's birthday was already quite steep, but scalpers have still seemingly managed to find buyers willing to spend thousands.

In the 24 hours since pre-order pages went live, multiple listings have popped up on eBay and, in many cases, successfully sold the Xbox Series X25 console bundle for more than $2,000. One scalper selling the full package – which Microsoft said comes with the "XBOX 25" branded 1TB console and controller, as well as a copy of Halo: Campaign Evolved – managed to successfully close a listing for $2,800. Many, many others have managed to sell their confirmed purchases for around $2,500.

That's a remarkable increase for an already pricey Xbox console, but the individual controller is getting hit just as hard. If you want to pick up one of the controllers (which also happen to have the original Xbox logo hidden in the back) from eBay, you could be spending as much as $185, more than double its retail cost. Many others are going for around $130.

"This collection is our way of celebrating the community that has made XBOX what it is today," Microsoft said when detailing its X25 collection earlier this week. "Thank you for being part of this journey."

Unfortunately, direct pre-orders for the release from retailers like Amazon and Best Buy seem to be largely sold out, at least for now. It's also not a surprise to see scalpers hitting the X25 collection as hard as they are. Valve's new Steam controller and Steam Machine were hit particularly hard when they launched earlier this year. Even the upcoming Grand Theft Auto 6 was hit by scalpers despite Rockstar Games confirming it will only release GTA 6 digitally.

The difference between the X25 release and things like Pokémon cards or the Steam Machine is there's no guarantee that Microsoft has any plans to produce more Xbox anniversary consoles. This seems like an extremely limited release, giving scalpers the perfect opportunity to strike while the iron's hot and make a quick buck. The company has also confirmed each console features its own unique engraving.

The Xbox 25th anniversary collection launches November 13, 2026, with its standalone controller set to arrive earlier come October 20. Target reportedly had some employees slicing open Pokémon card boxes to discourage scalping behavior earlier this month. One Disney store in London had to temporarily close after a few scalpers got "aggressive" toward others.

items.title: Nvidia's DLSS 5 Leaks Online, and Modders Have Already Turned It Into a Slop Filter
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Nvidia debuted DLSS 5 back in March 2026, promising to bring neural rendering to games in order to make them look more realistic. While pretty much everyone hated it, it seems like Nvidia has continued to work on it behind the scenes: It's leaked in a build of the NBA 2K27 beta.

Twitter user @renan_maniero spotted the new DLSS file in the NBA 2K27 early access, called nvngx_dlssnr.dll. The 'nr' at the end there appears to stand for neural rendering. Just finding the file in the game's directory would be one thing, but it looks like some enterprising modders have been able to build it into some other existing games.

Eita, o acesso antecipado do jogo NBA 2K27 veio com uma DLL nova do DLSS.

DLSS-NR (Neural Rendering) 👀 pic.twitter.com/X15fYO92RU

— Renan Maniero (@renan_maniero) August 26, 2026

Some modders built a DLSS 5 mod and integrated it into Control, which was spotted by Gizmodo. In the initial post on X, you can see the modders manipulating some sliders to change the degree by which the neural renderer is changing the image. Things like auto skin mask, intensity and style are all customizable, which is something Nvidia said would be possible when it announced the technology earlier this year.

A YouTube video shows the mod in action, and from the moment neural rendering is enabled, the frame rate is cut nearly in half – from 95fps to 53. Keep in mind that right now the mod is limited to character models, and it really only has the effect of making Jessie look like she needs a nap.

Over on the Nvidia subreddit, some modders were able to work the tech into The Last of Us Part 2, and while most of the images with the tech enabled make the characters look downright weird, the response seems to be split down the middle. One user says the DLSS 5 "looks deep fried, I am not going to lie," which is probably where I'm sitting. Someone else says, "There's more detail and the characters look more photo realistic and less like Pixar characters."

Obviously, this technology is in its very early stages, and once game developers are able to actually work it into the game naturally and optimize it, there probably won't be such a pronounced performance impact. But it's hard to imagine that turning on DLSS 5 will in any way improve your frame rate, which makes it one of the first pieces of Nvidia's AI software suite that makes performance worse.

Either way, now that the DLL file that enables the technology is clearly out in the wild, it's only a matter of time before it actually makes its way to market. But if the RTX 5090 gets its performance cut in half, I don't know if I'd recommend anyone enable it until some future graphics card hits the market.

Because while the visual effect the tech has will probably be debated until the end of time, the performance impact is where PC gamers tend to decide whether or not tech is worth using. It took a few years for people to start actually turning ray tracing on, as it was a surefire way to halve your performance in its early days. I'll be testing the technology one way or another as soon as Nvidia actually releases it.

Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

items.title: After GTA 6: Extended Look Showed Rockstar's Game Running at 30fps, Tech Experts Say a 60fps Console Version Is 'Extremely Unlikely' and 'Genuinely Challenging' Even on PC
items.description: Getting Rockstar's hugely ambitious GTA 6 running at 60fps on current consoles will be "extremely unlikely", the tech experts at Digital Foundry have said, after analysis of footage from the Grand Theft Auto 6: Extended Look.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Getting Rockstar's hugely ambitious GTA 6 running at 60fps on current consoles will be "extremely unlikely", the tech experts at Digital Foundry have said, after analysis of footage from the Grand Theft Auto 6: Extended Look.

Yesterday's 27-minute reveal featured 30fps footage of the game on Netflix, YouTube, and in the raw file made available by Rockstar to download — and this is seemingly how we should all expect the game to look when it arrives on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S this November.

While 30fps might seem low compared to the frame counts of other modern gaming blockbusters, Rockstar appears to be targeting this level to maximize the sheer detail on offer in every one of those frames, Digital Foundry believes.

"It's clear that the focus was absolutely maximising the level of visual detail at a fixed 30fps frame-rate on all platforms," Digital Foundry wrote in an Extended Look deep dive article. "The rendering, simulation and presentation have all been tuned around that constraint - and the result is an unprecedented level of density, material quality and world coherence, with trade-offs landing primarily in image quality and animation smoothness rather than systemic scale or fidelity."

Specifically, the report goes on to heap praise on GTA 6's character rendering, including skin shading that makes sweat and make-up look convincing, and "huge generation improvements to hair simulation" that allows Lucia's locks to behave realistically with convincing snap-back motions, delayed follow-through and impressive "base-to-tip motion."

In terms of resolution, Digital Foundry suspects the PS5's internal rendering is clocked at 1440p without DRS, without any strong evidence of FSR 2 or TAA upscaling being used. This can lead to "a degree of softness, visible geometric aliasing and shimmer on fine details," Digital Foundry wrote, but no sign of frame-rate drops that have hampered previous entries in the series at launch. While improvements for the beefier PS5 Pro are only speculative, improved image quality and ray-tracing were mooted as more likely, over any transformative boost in performance.

"The evidence suggests that the game maintains its 33.3ms cadence with care, and Rockstar has clearly spent immense effort balancing CPU and GPU workloads to fully saturate the hardware," Digital Foundry continued. "That makes a 60fps version extremely unlikely on console hardware - there's no way to regain enough GPU and particularly CPU time to make a 16.7ms update rate work without compromising the world."

The game is carefully balanced in terms of its ambition, then, with the downside that there's likely little left in the tank to enable a 60fps mode down the line — at least on the current crop of consoles. But how about PC?

"Looking ahead to other console versions and the presumably-coming-eventually PC release, some level of caution is required," Digital Foundry wrote. "The PC platform ought to allow for higher resolutions, especially with the benefit of more modern temporal upscalers like DLSS, alongside increased RT sample counts, longer draw distances and so on. However, the CPU demands of a world this complex - tuned around console Zen 2 cores at 30fps - could make hitting 60fps genuinely challenging in a way we don't often see, and will likely require a high-end CPU like a recent Ryzen X3D to avoid bottlenecks."

IGN is one of the very few outlets to have been given an exclusive preview of GTA 6. We also have details on GTA 6's romance system, how long GTA 6 will take to beat, every GTA 6 side activity we've spotted so far, and how GTA 6's bigger map compares to past Rockstar games as part of our exhaustive and ongoing coverage. Up to speed on all that? Here's 69 new gameplay details we spotted during our time with GTA 6.

While improvements for the beefier PS5 Pro are only speculative, improved image quality and ray-tracing were mooted as more likely, over any transformative boost in performance.

"The evidence suggests that the game maintains its 33.3ms cadence with care, and Rockstar has clearly spent immense effort balancing CPU and GPU workloads to fully saturate the hardware," Digital Foundry continued. "That makes a 60fps version extremely unlikely on console hardware - there's no way to regain enough GPU and particularly CPU time to make a 16.7ms update rate work without compromising the world."

The game is carefully balanced in terms of its ambition, then, with the downside that there's likely little left in the tank to enable a 60fps mode down the line — at least on the current crop of consoles. But how about PC?

"Looking ahead to other console versions and the presumably-coming-eventually PC release, some level of caution is required," Digital Foundry wrote. "The PC platform ought to allow for higher resolutions, especially with the benefit of more modern temporal upscalers like DLSS, alongside increased RT sample counts, longer draw distances and so on. However, the CPU demands of a world this complex - tuned around console Zen 2 cores at 30fps - could make hitting 60fps genuinely challenging in a way we don't often see, and will likely require a high-end CPU like a recent Ryzen X3D to avoid bottlenecks."

IGN is one of the very few outlets to have been given an exclusive preview of GTA 6. We also have details on GTA 6's romance system, how long GTA 6 will take to beat, every GTA 6 side activity we've spotted so far, and how GTA 6's bigger map compares to past Rockstar games as part of our exhaustive and ongoing coverage. items.title: Jeremy Renner Teases Hawkeye Return as Avengers: Doomsday Reshoots Reportedly Underway
items.description: Hawkeye star Jeremy Renner appears to be teasing a long-awaited return to the MCU, as a final round of Avengers: Doomsday reshoots reportedly gets underway.
items.author: Tom Phillips
items.content:
Hawkeye star Jeremy Renner appears to be teasing a long-awaited return to the MCU, as a final round of Avengers: Doomsday reshoots reportedly gets underway.

Renner posted what appeared to be a clear tease for his involvement via Instagram today, with a photo of his Hawkeye costume set to the "Hawkeye Theme" music.

The timing of this post is very interesting, as it follows confirmation this week from M'Baku actor Winston Duke, who stated that "additional photography for Avengers: Doomsday" is now underway, per an interview with CNA.

Of course, Avengers: Doomsday is now just four months from launch — meaning that any additional material shot now has a just limited time to be worked into the production. But Marvel seems to have planned for this situation, with filming essentially tacked on to the start of filming for 2027's Avengers: Secret Wars, which is expected to begin its own production shoot in September.

Indeed, it's likely that any additional work on Doomsday at this stage will be for shorter scenes or smaller moments, rather than any major alterations to Doomsday's plot. Comments from Marvel tipster Daniel Richtman, who has a decent track record reporting MCU leaks, suggest that this filming will be used to "add a lot of cameos" — of which OG Avenger Hawkeye is presumably one.

After appearances in numerous MCU films, audiences last saw Renner as Hawkeye in the enjoyable Disney+ TV series of the same name, where he mentored Hailee Steinfeld's Kate Bishop and saved the day just in time for Christmas. Since then, Renner has been recovering from injuries sustained during his serious snowplough accident in January 2023, and said he had turned down a subsequent offer to return for a second season of Hawkeye due to a disagreement with Disney over pay.

"They asked me to do Season 2, and they offered me half the money. I’m like, ‘Well, it’s going to take me twice the amount of work for half the amount of money, and eight months of my time, essentially, to do it for half the amount," Renner claimed.

"I'm like, 'I'm sorry? Why? Did you think I’m only half the Jeremy because I got ran over? Maybe that's why you want to pay me half of what I made on the first season.' This is not Marvel, mind you. This is like, just Disney, not even really Disney. It’s just the penny pinchers, the accountants. I told them to go fly a kite. I mean, just at the insult offer. So we didn’t see eye to eye on it."

Thankfully, Renner suggested he was still open to appearing as Hawkeye again, just not in those circumstances. And now, it seems, we may get one more appearance from the Avengers' best archer, at least.

Avengers: Doomsday is finally set to arrive in theaters on December 18, and even without Renner and the addition of further cameos, boasts one of the most stacked movie casts of all time. Fan interest and excitement for Avengers: Doomsday has been strong, with ticket pre-sales shifting faster than those for Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Looking for more ways to get ready? Despite saying that Avengers: Doomsday would reset the MCU to 'Phase Zero', Marvel has released a watchlist of 15 movies and TV shows you should watch before Avengers: Doomsday rolls around.

Images credit: Marvel, Jeremy Renner/Instagram
